title: The Prince Sets Sail for Home

scenes.title: Athena Wakes Telemachus
scenes.card: In Sparta, the goddess warns the king's son to sail home at once and avoid the suitors' ambush.

subs.text: Book fifteen.
The Prince Sets Sail for Home.
Scene one.
Athena Wakes Telemachus.
Telemachus, wake.
It is wrong to wander while your house is eaten hollow.
Go home now,
before your mother's own kin bend her to marry Eurymachus and your inheritance walks out the door with her.
And hear this too:
the boldest of the suitors lie in ambush in the strait between Ithaca and rocky Same,
hungry for your blood before you ever reach home.
Keep clear of that channel, sail wide, and sail by night.
When you touch Ithaca, send ship and crew round to the town without you.
Go first, on foot, to the swineherd Eumaeus, who keeps faith with your house;
sleep there, and send him to tell your mother you are safely home.
Telemachus wakes Pisistratus and prepares to depart at dawn.

scenes.title: Farewell from Menelaus and Helen
scenes.card: The son leaves the king and queen of Sparta with gifts; a bird sign suggests his father's revenge is near.

subs.text: Scene two.
Farewell from Menelaus and Helen.
Menelaus, dear to Zeus, your gifts honor me and I take them gladly.
But do not hold me for more feasting;
my heart is already on Ithaca, and I fear what rots there while I linger.
Take this robe, child, woven by my own hands, for the bride you will one day wed;
let your mother keep it till then.
And read that eagle with the white goose in its claws as I do:
so Odysseus, home from long wandering, will stoop upon the suitors, or he is home already, seeding their ruin.
So the whips came down and the horses flew, through Phera as the sun set, and on to sandy Pylos with the dawn.
Son of Nestor, will you do me one kindness more, and drive me past your father's gates,
straight down to my ship?
Old Nestor's welcome is warm, but it does not let go, and I cannot lose a night to it.

scenes.title: Theoclymenus Joins the Voyage
scenes.card: At the harbor, the son takes aboard a fugitive prophet and sails through the night toward Ithaca.

subs.text: Scene three.
Theoclymenus Joins the Voyage.
Aboard, men, rig the mast and run out the oars.
We sail for home now, not at dawn.
Friend, by your sacrifice and by the god you pour to, tell me truly who you are, and then hear me.
I have killed a kinsman in Argos, and his brothers hunt my life across the islands.
Take me aboard, for I am a suppliant and a seer, and I have nowhere on this earth to stand.
I will not push away a man who asks.
Come aboard;
you'll share what we have, and in Ithaca you will be made welcome.
Grey-eyed Athena sent the wind astern, and the black ship ran through the dark,
past Elis and the needle islands, toward Ithaca and the ambush that waited in the strait.

scenes.title: Eumaeus Tells His Own Story
scenes.card: At the hut, the swineherd tells the beggar how he was kidnapped as a child and raised in Odysseus's family.

subs.text: Scene four.
Eumaeus Tells His Own Story.
At dawn, friend, I'll go down to the town and beg at the great house;
perhaps the suitors need a man to carve meat and pour wine.
I refuse to eat your bread another day and give nothing back.
Tell me of old Laertes, does he still live?
And the mother of Odysseus, what became of her?
And you yourself, friend:
what land bore you, and how did you come to serve this house?
I was a king's son once, on the island men call Syria,
till a Phoenician woman of my father's house sold me to her traders for trinkets and a passage home.
Seven days we ran before the wind;
on the seventh she dropped dead in the hold, and they carried me on like cargo, to sell.
Laertes bought him in Ithaca and the royal household raised him.

scenes.title: Telemachus Lands in Secret
scenes.card: A hawk kills a dove, which the prophet reads as good news; the son lands secretly and walks toward the swineherd's farm.

subs.text: Scene five.
Telemachus Lands in Secret.
And as the ship closed on Ithaca, a hawk, Apollo's swift messenger,
swept by on the right with a dove torn in its talons, and the feathers fell between Telemachus and the sea.
The bird flew on your right hand, Telemachus, no house in Ithaca out-kings yours;
the power stays with your line forever!
Crew, take her round to the town harbor without me;
I go inland to look over my farms.
Tonight I lodge with the herdsmen, and tomorrow evening I'll set out a feast to pay you for the voyage.
Piraeus will keep you honorably, friend, until I send for you.
Trust him as you would me.
